To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the new generation of parity violating electron scattering (PVES) experiments will probe the electroweak sector of the Standard Model at the 1-10% level, (ii) the sensitivity of PVES to physics beyond the Standard Model is comparable to that of other precision measurements, and (iii) the new generation PVES experiments will provide a new window into the physics of the electroweaks sector.
the experimental results to date are in good agreement with the Standard Model predictions and the future measurements have great potential for discovering new physics.

the recent results of the Qweak experiment at Jefferson Lab have shown that the weak charge of the proton, and hence the weak mixing angle, are in agreement with Standard Model expectations, and that the future P2 experiment will measure the weak charges of the neutron and deuteron, and hence the electroweak parameters of the neutron and the weak charge of a free neutron, with unprecedented precision.

the search for new physics beyond the Standard Model.
the search for new physics beyond the standard model of electroweak interactions.
the physics of the electroweak interactions of leptons and quarks.
